linkedin: Want to increase your chances of getting read in a remote job application? When hiring managers read applications on a screen, between meetings, often in a second language, they look for ones that are easy to scan and clearly written for the role. To stand out, follow these tips: lead with the job title and a brief summary of your relevant experience, show proof of async work by mentioning a project with written updates or a time zone gap you handled well, match the job post's language, keep your CV short and current with your most recent remote or freelance work first, and follow up once politely if you hear nothing after a week. Additionally, only include a photo if the job post asks for one, and consider a short cover letter if the post asks a direct question you can answer. Even without remote experience, you can point to work with written communication and little supervision. carousel.title: Make it easy to scan
carousel.body: Remote hiring managers read applications on a screen, between meetings, often in a second language. They look for ones that are easy to scan and clearly written for the role.

carousel.title: Lead with the role
carousel.body: Open with the exact job title and where you saw it. Then say in one sentence why your recent work fits what the team does.

carousel.title: Show async work proof
carousel.body: Mention a project you ran with written updates, a shared document you owned, or a time zone gap you handled well.

carousel.title: Match the job post
carousel.body: Read the job post twice. If they say 'customer support', do not write 'client care'.
